condition: Acute pancreatitis presenting as a raised lipase
summary: 52-year-old man sent in by his GP with a lipase of 820 U/L taken for two days of vague epigastric discomfort.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Raised lipase on a blood test
inputs.hpi: GP bloods for two days of vague upper abdominal discomfort after a weekend of heavy drinking. Discomfort now constant in the epigastrium, going through to the back, with nausea. No vomiting of blood, no jaundice, no fever. Drinks about 40 units a week.

exam.abdomen: Epigastric tenderness, no guarding or peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

inputs.socialHistory: Drinks about 40 units of alcohol a week. Smoker, 20 a day.

mustNotMiss.note: A raised lipase also comes with perforated ulcer, mesenteric ischaemia and a leaking aneurysm: at least one should stay on the list until examined or imaged.

guideline.name: Revised Atlanta classification of acute pancreatitis
guideline.section: Diagnosis: two of typical pain, lipase or amylase at least three times the upper limit of normal, characteristic imaging

rationale: Entry point: a laboratory result. The loop starts from the raised lipase (reverse index), goes back to the history (typical pain, alcohol) and the examination, then forward; Atlanta 2 of 3 is met with typical pain and lipase ≥ 3 × ULN.

authoring.author: Claude (vademecum phase 1, entry-point pilot)
authoring.notes: Starts from a result (laboratory, imaging or pathology), not a complaint. Written for the vademecum shadow (clinval:web --engine vademecum); not verified on iOS; clinical sign-off pending (docs/clinical-validation/changes/vademecum-phase1.md).
